1.w: “But now they mock me, those who are younger than I, whose fathers I disdained too much to put with my sheep dogs.

2.w: Moreover, the strength of their hands— what use was it to me? Those whose strength had perished,

3.w: gaunt with want and hunger, they would roam the parched land, by night a desolate waste.

4.w: By the brush they would gather herbs from the salt marshes, and the root of the broom tree was their food.

5.w: They were banished from the community — people shouted at them as they would shout at thieves —

6.w: so that they had to live in the dry stream beds, in the holes of the ground, and among the rocks.

7.w: They brayed like animals among the bushes and were huddled together under the nettles.

8.w: Sons of senseless and nameless people, they were driven out of the land with whips.

9.w: “And now I have become their taunt song; I have become a byword among them.

10.w: They detest me and maintain their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

11.w: Because God has untied my tent cord and afflicted me, people throw off all restraint in my presence.

12.w: On my right the young rabble rise up; they drive me from place to place and build up siege ramps against me.

13.w: They destroy my path; they succeed in destroying me without anyone assisting them.

14.w: They come in as through a wide breach; amid the crash they come rolling in.

15.w: Terrors are turned loose on me; they drive away my honor like the wind, and as a cloud my deliverance has passed away.

16.w: “And now my soul pours itself out within me; days of suffering take hold of me.

17.w: Night pierces my bones; my gnawing pains never cease.

18.w: With great power God grasps my clothing; he binds me like the collar of my tunic.

19.w: He has flung me into the mud, and I have come to resemble dust and ashes.

20.w: I cry out to you, but you do not answer me; I stand up, and you only look at me.

21.w: You have become cruel to me; with the strength of your hand you attack me.

22.w: You pick me up on the wind and make me ride on it; you toss me about in the storm.

23.w: I know that you are bringing me to death, to the meeting place for all the living.

24.w: “Surely one does not stretch out his hand against a broken man when he cries for help in his distress.

25.w: Have I not wept for the unfortunate? Was not my soul grieved for the poor?

26.w: But when I hoped for good, trouble came; when I expected light, then darkness came.

27.w: My heart is in turmoil unceasingly; the days of my affliction confront me.

28.w: I go about blackened, but not by the sun; in the assembly I stand up and cry for help.

29.w: I have become a brother to jackals and a companion of ostriches.

30.w: My skin has turned dark on me; my body is hot with fever.

31.w: My harp is used for mourning and my flute for the sound of weeping.
